injuryReports.returnComment: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuryReports.returnComment: Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been held under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Egbuka brought in two of five targets for 18 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Baker Mayfield
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Mayfield completed 20 of 33 passes for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 36 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay.

injuryReports.name: Bucky Irving
injuryReports.returnComment: Irving worked hard all afternoon against a feisty Lions defense, and outside of his game-long 23-yard run, he scuffled to 45 yards on 17 carries. Irving worked around a hard shot to the abdomen that he sustained in the second half, and he did manage to contribute a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game when he went in from one yard out in the latter portion of the third quarter. Irving has now equaled a career high with eight rushing touchdowns, and he's 107 yards short of his second career 1,000-yard season on the ground heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 32 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cor'Dale Flott
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Terrell Burgess
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: John Franklin-Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Franklin-Myers' practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a lingering back issue, but his full session Thursday puts the veteran defensive lineman on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Jaguars. Franklin-Myers is off to a disappointing start to his Titans tenure, with the 2018 fourth-rounder accumulating 18 tackles (seven solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Franklin-Myers (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Dorian Mausi
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Tony Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Adams has recovered from the illness that sidelined him for the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Cowboys. The safety has already returned to full practice participation and should be all set to continue stringing together prep sessions in anticipation of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Adams (illness) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Kylen Granson
injuryReports.returnComment: Granson displayed some pass-catching ability in his first five seasons in the league between stops with the Colts and Eagles, but the Titans have deployed him almost exclusively on special teams in 2026. He's been active for just four of the team's first 10 contests and has drawn just one target while playing three total snaps on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Granson logged all 16 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: David Martin-Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: The third-year tight end out of Temple is a core contributor on special teams but has been an afterthought on offense throughout the season. Martin-Robinson hasn't played double-digit snaps on offense in any of his nine appearances and has yet to draw a target.
injuryReports.injury: Martin-Robinson played all but one of his 24 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Winston Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winston was able to register at least seven stops for the sixth time this season while playing every defensive snap in Week 11. The safety has now compiled 63 total tackles (35 solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery over eight contests so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Winston recorded seven total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Cedric Gray
injuryReports.returnComment: Gray finished second on the Titans in tackles behind Joshua Williams (11) in a game that saw Tennessee's defense yield six consecutive touchdown drives to Dallas. Gray has recorded eight stops in back-to-back outings and is up to 54 tackles (30 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).
injuryReports.injury: Gray posted eight tackles (four solo) during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The Titans' defense failed to put up much of a fight against the Cowboys, who scored touchdowns on each of their first six offensive drives. Williams led Tennessee with a career-high 11 stops, and it was the first time he reached double-digits tackles in a game since entering the league as a fourth-round selection of the Chiefs in the 2022 NFL Draft. He's up to 33 tackles (22 solo) and two pass defenses across five regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Wiliams posted 11 tackles (nine solo) during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Corey Thornton
injuryReports.returnComment: Starting corner Cor'Dale Flott suffered a neck injury during Sunday's game at Dallas, which could be part of the reason the Titans are looking to add depth in their secondary. Over two games with the Panthers this season, Thornton recorded eight tackles (six solo) and an interception.
injuryReports.injury: Tennessee signed Thornton (fibula) off the Panthers' practice squad Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Daniel Bellinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end capitalized on his sole target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.
injuryReports.injury: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Restrepo
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26). Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.
injuryReports.injury: Restrepo caught his lone target for five yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Michael Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: With Tyjae Spears (knee) back on the shelf and sent to injured reserve over the weekend, Carter played 14 of 68 offensive snaps behind Tony Pollard in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Carter ended up carrying the ball four times for nine yards and caught his lone target for two yards. He should remain Pollard's backup for at least the next three games while Spears is out, unless the Titans have a change of heart and want to start getting rookie Nicholas Singleton some playing time.
injuryReports.injury: Carter reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Elic Ayomanor
injuryReports.returnComment: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps also were third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.
injuryReports.injury: Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Joey Slye
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran kicker made field goals from 38, 48 and 28 yards in the first half and is in the midst of a career-best season. He's now 18-for-19 on field-goal tries and has made all 17 PATs through 10 games. Kicking in one of the lower-scoring offenses in the league, it still doesn't translate to much fantasy appeal for Slye ahead of next Sunday's road date with the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Slye made all three field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Gunnar Helm
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Chimere Dike
injuryReports.returnComment: Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Calvin Ridley
injuryReports.returnComment: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Cam Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Carnell Tate
injuryReports.returnComment: Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Tate brought in two of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Amik Robertson
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Stefon Diggs
injuryReports.returnComment: Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.
injuryReports.injury: Diggs (personal) was removed from the Commanders' injury report Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Treylon Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been listed on Commanders practice reports with a foot injury since Week 8, but he's missed only one contest (Week 9 against the Rams) in four chances during that span. Friday's report will determine if Burks has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Arizona.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Charles Omenihu
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: John Bates
injuryReports.returnComment: Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: Bates didn't garner a target during Monday night's 22-20 win over the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Ben Sinnott
injuryReports.returnComment: Chig Okonkwo was the Commanders' only tight end who produced offensively Monday, with the fifth-year pro catching four of five passes for 66 yards. Sinnott has been targeted zero times in seven of 10 regular-season games, with his lone productive outing being Week 10 against the Giants, when he brought in all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He brings very little fantasy appeal heading into Washington's Week 12 road tilt against Arizona on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Sinnott played played 33 snaps (24 on offense, nine on special teams) but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Van Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jefferson could not hold onto a deep pass from Jayden Daniels early in the fourth quarter, and that catch would have set up the Commanders in the red zone. Jefferson has seen only one pass across his two outings since putting together a 5-58-1 receiving line on seven targets against the Rams in Week 9. Jefferson is firmly entrenched as the Commanders' WR4 behind Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks heading into Week 12 against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Jefferson failed to haul in his lone target during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Drew Stevens
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevens had himself a career night in Week 11. The kicker made all five field goals in the second half, converting attempts from 36, 40, 25 and 41 yards before nailing a 26-yard game winner as time expired in regulation. Stevens has now gone 22-for-25 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-7 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 19 extra-point attempts over the first 10 games of his rookie campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Stevens went 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Monday night's 22-20 win over the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Austin Ekeler
injuryReports.returnComment: Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a four-game absence due to a groin injury and finished Monday's game with 13 carries for 54 yards. Despite his return, Ekeler ended up with the second-most carries on the Commanders while Rachaad White -- who led Washington's backfield in Croskey-Merritt's absence -- didn't get a single touch on offense. It appears as though Ekeler is the preferred change-of-pace back in Washington's offense heading into Week 12 against Arizona.
injuryReports.injury: Ekeler turned seven carries into 41 yards and caught two of three targets for three yards during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Rachaad White
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: White turned two kickoff returns into 48 yards during Monday's 22-20 win over the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuryReports.returnComment: Okonkwo contributed his game-long 32-yard grab on his first catch of the night, and the veteran tight end went on to finish second in receiving yards for the Commanders. He also contributed a key 13-yard grab on Washington's penultimate drive that culminated in a key field goal, and in all, three of his four receptions resulted in first downs. Okonkwo has at least four catches in three straight games but still is seeking his first touchdown of the season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Okonkwo brought in four of five targets for 66 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.
injuryReports.injury: Williams brought in nine of 11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Croskey-Merritt outpaced Austin Ekeler, the only other Commanders back to log a carry, by six rush attempts. The second-year pro also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 12 seconds remaining in the first half. Croskey-Merritt averaged over 4.0 yards per carry for the second straight game after failing to eclipse that mark in each of the first four games of the season, and he should be in store for an even busier day in a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 23 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added six carries for 55 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Lucas Patrick
injuryReports.returnComment: Patrick has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in time for Monday night's contest. Patrick will step back into his starting center role against an improved Bengals defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Patrick (concussion) is active for Monday night's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Quan Martin
injuryReports.returnComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Laremy Tunsil
injuryReports.returnComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
injuryReports.injury: Triceps

injuryReports.name: Colson Yankoff
injuryReports.returnComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Luke McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Reaves
injuryReports.returnComment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nick Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).

sources.name: Antonio Williams
sources.returnComment: The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. sources.name: Jayden Daniels
sources.returnComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

qbChemistry.method: Starter-linked weekly statistics; starting QB must supply at least 80% of team attempts and 15 attempts. Two-year recency half-life, eight-game pair and five-game comparison shrinkage; maximum 15% receiving change. Target allocation is conserved within each forecast team. No unsupported same-QB sample means no chemistry adjustment.
limitations: Starter-linked team-game splits are observational, not exact passer-target charting.
Role, opponent and scheme differences can confound historical splits.
Not yet validated out of sample; adjusted markets cannot pass the betting quality gate.

lineupPolicy.scope: Future forecast eligibility only. Missing rows are not actual zeros. No scoring probability or void-bet outcome is invented.

tdReport.orderMethodology: First and last TD fair odds come from separate player-game models trained on actual first/last scorer IDs, including defensive/return TDs in the event order and overtime. They use lagged opportunity and prior scoring-order rates; ATTD probabilities are not reused as first/last estimates. Game-level probability caps reserve mass for unmodeled scorers and no-TD outcomes. Book settlement rules may differ.
